body.v: Great, that works for me. I have put the final figures into CloudDrive so we can both edit them. It will ask you to sign in with your work email.
You wrote on Monday: "Send me the figures when they are final and I will check them."

hotspots.explain: The address really is Elena's and the thread is real. A hijacked account passes every address check.
A new shared file that needs you to sign in with your work email is how a login gets copied.
clouddrive-view.example is not CloudDrive's domain, clouddrive.example. A thief using Elena's account can send any link.
Quoting your own words makes it feel real, but whoever reads the inbox can copy them.

who.prompt: Who is really writing to you? Look at the address, not just the name.
who.answer: Possibly not Elena. The address and the thread are real, so her account may have been taken over. Only a call can tell.
choices: Maybe Elena, maybe someone using her hijacked account
Definitely Elena, since the thread is real

emotion.prompt: What feeling is this email trying to create?
emotion.answer: Helpfulness and a little hurry to finish the report together.
choices: A wish to help finish the report

ask.prompt: What exactly does it want you to do?
ask.answer: Sign in to CloudDrive through a link, which would give your work login to whoever controls Elena's account.
choices: Reply with your date of birth

verify.prompt: How can you check through a channel you control?
verify.answer: Do not use the link. Open CloudDrive yourself and look for the file, or call Elena on a number you already know.
choices: Open CloudDrive yourself, or call Elena on a known number
Sign in, since the thread is real
Reply to ask if it is her

actions.label: Open CloudDrive yourself and look for the file, or call Elena
actions.consequence: No such file exists. Elena knows nothing about the email.

actions.label: Click the link and sign in
actions.consequence: The page copies your work login for whoever controls Elena's account.

actions.label: Reply and ask "Is this really you?"
actions.consequence: Whoever controls the account answers yes. You only asked the impostor.

actions.label: Tell IT that Elena's account may be taken over
actions.consequence: Good call. The account can be locked before it reaches more people.

attacker_reveal: A new kind of file-sharing email, in a thread you trusted, from someone you trust... You had never seen this exact trick, but the question was the same as ever: who is really writing, and how can you check?
